absent: Numeric values of thread flag bits, preempt count offsets and hardware interrupt state words.
Register frame layout and saved interrupt flag accessors.
Core implementations behind affinity moving, handler installation, deferred timer rearm and restartable-sequence handling.
Validation, tracing, context tracking, sanitiser, RCU and scheduler interactions beyond call sites.
Interrupt domain hierarchy, number allocation and controller callback contracts beyond signatures.
Tickless mask management and deferred wakeup flushing details.

findings.text: Three headers use single define guards to make repeated inclusion harmless. The guards are __LINUX_INTERRUPT_RC_H and __LINUX_IRQENTRYCOMMON_H plus _LINUX_IRQ_H.

Fallback interrupt probing uses probe_irq_on and probe_irq_off plus probe_irq_mask, with init_irq_proc for setup. The start helper yields zero, the stop and mask helpers each yield zero for any input, and the setup helper performs no action.

Two annotation macros steer emitted code into dedicated entry text sections. One macro named __irq_entry groups general interrupt entry code, while __softirq_entry groups soft interrupt entry code, keeping entry code separate from normal text.

Local interrupt masking uses a nesting count with per-CPU flag storage. Disabling via local_interrupt_disable saves processor flags then bumps the count through hardirq_disable_enter and records flags through _local_interrupt_save_state only on the outermost transition. Enabling via local_interrupt_enable drops the count through hardirq_disable_exit and restores through _local_interrupt_enable only when returning to unmasked. Inner helpers __local_interrupt_save_state and __local_interrupt_enable access the per-CPU slot.

Entry records the interrupts-off transition for validation and tracing, while exit paths demand hardware interrupts already off. Preparation and validation for user return plus both user and kernel exit wrappers assert the disabled state before proceeding. The no-op validation build defines lockdep and trace helpers as empty.

Entry from user mode via enter_from_user_mode establishes kernel accounting before handling. It invokes arch_enter_from_user_mode, marks interrupts off for validation, checks context state, leaves user context with interrupts off, then performs register sanitising and trace completion inside an instrumented window. The wrapper irqentry_enter_from_user_mode adds a restartable-sequence note of user interrupt entry.

Return to user mode runs preparation under disabled interrupts followed by validation and final transition. Preparation via __exit_to_user_mode_prepare flushes tickless wakeups, reads thread flags and handles deferred work under a caller supplied mask before an architecture hook. Syscall and interrupt wrappers named syscall_exit_to_user_mode_prepare and irqentry_exit_to_user_mode_prepare differ only in mask choice, each adding restartable-sequence handling and validation. Final step via exit_to_user_mode resets unwind info, prepares tracing, enters user context and performs architecture exit with interrupt-on accounting.

User-exit work is a union of thread flag contributions plus architecture additions. The base macro EXIT_TO_USER_MODE_WORK covers pending signals, resume notification, uprobes, eager rescheduling, lazy rescheduling, patch pending, signal notification, restartable sequences and ARCH_EXIT_TO_USER_MODE_WORK. Both _TIF_PATCH_PENDING and the default ARCH_EXIT_TO_USER_MODE_WORK are zero. Syscall exits use the base union in both build variants, while interrupt exits add a timer rearm contribution in one variant and use the base union alone in the other.

Kernel entry outcome uses irqentry_state with alias irqentry_state_t. It holds a two-way union where one member records whether context tracking was entered and the other records validation tracking, so only one boolean view is used at a time.

Kernel-mode entry via irqentry_enter_from_kernel_mode returns a flag telling exit whether context tracking was entered. Idle tasks or architectures reporting quiescent state through arch_in_rcu_eqs take a context-entering branch that marks interrupts off, enters interrupt context, sanitises registers and finishes tracing under instrumentation, setting the flag. Other contexts only mark interrupts off, sanitise registers, perform a tick check and finish tracing, leaving the flag clear. Tiny RCU builds drop the first branch at compile time.

Kernel-mode exit via irqentry_exit_to_kernel_mode sequences a preempt consideration with a restore stage. The preempt stage skips when saved registers had interrupts off or when context was entered, and otherwise triggers conditional rescheduling only when preemption is enabled. The restore stage rearms deferred timers when registers had interrupts on, completing tracer preparation plus context exit when the entered flag is set or tracing alone when clear. When registers had interrupts off it only completes context exit if the flag is set.

Interrupt sense values and descriptor property bits are fixed. IRQ_TYPE_NONE is zero and IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING is one while IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_FALLING is two, with IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH combining rising with falling. IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH is four and IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_LOW is eight, with IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_MASK combining both levels. IRQ_TYPE_SENSE_MASK covers the low nibble and IRQ_TYPE_DEFAULT equals that mask, while IRQ_TYPE_PROBE is sixteen. Properties place IRQ_LEVEL at bit eight and IRQ_PER_CPU at nine, IRQ_NOPROBE at ten, IRQ_NOREQUEST at eleven, IRQ_NOAUTOEN at twelve, IRQ_NO_BALANCING at thirteen with fourteen unused, IRQ_NESTED_THREAD at fifteen, IRQ_NOTHREAD at sixteen, IRQ_PER_CPU_DEVID at seventeen, IRQ_IS_POLLED at eighteen, IRQ_DISABLE_UNLAZY at nineteen, IRQ_HIDDEN at twenty, IRQ_NO_DEBUG at twenty-one and IRQ_RESERVED at twenty-two.

Derived interrupt masks and affinity outcome codes are fixed. IRQF_MODIFY_MASK groups sense bits with no-probe, no-request, no-auto-enable, level, no-balancing, per-CPU, nested thread, no-thread, per-CPU device id, polled, disable-unlazily and hidden properties. IRQ_NO_BALANCING_MASK groups per-CPU with no-balancing. Outcomes place IRQ_SET_MASK_OK at zero with IRQ_SET_MASK_OK_NOCOPY at one and IRQ_SET_MASK_OK_DONE at two.

Shared interrupt bookkeeping named irq_common_data carries a private state word plus handler linkage and optional placement data. It holds handler_data with msi_desc, plus node when NUMA is on and affinity on multiprocessor builds, alongside effective_affinity when that option is on and ipi_offset when that option is on.

Per-chip interrupt data named irq_data links identities to controller objects. It references common bookkeeping with chip and domain, plus an optional parent_data link in hierarchical domains. It also carries logical irq with hardware hwirq numbers, a mask word and chip_data for controller private use.

Per-interrupt state bit positions are fixed. IRQD_TRIGGER_MASK covers the low four bits. Single bits place IRQD_SETAFFINITY_PENDING at eight with IRQD_ACTIVATED at nine, IRQD_NO_BALANCING at ten, IRQD_PER_CPU at eleven, IRQD_AFFINITY_SET at twelve, IRQD_LEVEL at thirteen, IRQD_WAKEUP_STATE at fourteen with fifteen unused, IRQD_IRQ_DISABLED at sixteen, IRQD_IRQ_MASKED at seventeen, IRQD_IRQ_INPROGRESS at eighteen, IRQD_WAKEUP_ARMED at nineteen, IRQD_FORWARDED_TO_VCPU at twenty, IRQD_AFFINITY_MANAGED at twenty-one, IRQD_IRQ_STARTED at twenty-two, IRQD_MANAGED_SHUTDOWN at twenty-three, IRQD_SINGLE_TARGET at twenty-four, IRQD_DEFAULT_TRIGGER_SET at twenty-five, IRQD_CAN_RESERVE at twenty-six, IRQD_HANDLE_ENFORCE_IRQCTX at twenty-seven, IRQD_AFFINITY_ON_ACTIVATE at twenty-eight, IRQD_IRQ_ENABLED_ON_SUSPEND at twenty-nine and IRQD_RESEND_WHEN_IN_PROGRESS at thirty with thirty-one unused.

Small helpers query or update single state bits without exposing the word directly. They report pending affinity, per-CPU nature, balance eligibility as neither per-CPU nor no-balancing, affinity and trigger history, level type, single target, enforced context, suspend and wakeup settings, masked with progress and armed states, activation with start and managed shutdown, reservation eligibility, activate-time affinity and resend need. Mutators record affinity history and replace the trigger nibble while marking default trigger set, with paired setters and clearers for activation and reservation.

Controller interface named irq_chip is a name with flags plus optional callbacks grouped by purpose. Lifecycle covers startup with shutdown and enable with disable plus suspend with resume and power shutdown. Masking covers acknowledge with mask and mask-with-acknowledge plus unmask and end of interrupt. Configuration covers affinity with pre-redirect and retrigger plus type and wake with bus lock and unlock, alongside deferred move completion, mask calculation, chip printing and resource acquire with release. Messaging covers message compose with write plus single and mask sends. State covers chip state get with set and virtual CPU affinity, while non-maskable support covers setup with teardown.

Controller capability bits and build defaults are fixed. IRQCHIP_SET_TYPE_MASKED sits at bit zero with IRQCHIP_EOI_IF_HANDLED at one, IRQCHIP_MASK_ON_SUSPEND at two, IRQCHIP_ONOFFLINE_ENABLED at three, IRQCHIP_SKIP_SET_WAKE at four, IRQCHIP_ONESHOT_SAFE at five, IRQCHIP_EOI_THREADED at six, IRQCHIP_SUPPORTS_LEVEL_MSI at seven, IRQCHIP_SUPPORTS_NMI at eight, IRQCHIP_ENABLE_WAKEUP_ON_SUSPEND at nine, IRQCHIP_AFFINITY_PRE_STARTUP at ten, IRQCHIP_IMMUTABLE at eleven and IRQCHIP_MOVE_DEFERRED at twelve. NR_IRQS_LEGACY with ARCH_IRQ_INIT_FLAGS and IRQ_DEFAULT_INIT_FLAGS are all zero, and irq_affinity_online_cpu is null in this configuration.

Affinity moving via irq_move_irq with irq_move_masked_irq, plus irq_can_move_in_process_context, parent assignment via irq_set_parent, and handler installation via irq_set_chip_and_handler with irq_set_chained_handler are thin wrappers. One move variant forwards only when affinity is pending while the alternate build provides empty moves and always reports process-context moves allowed. Parent assignment reports success without action. Chip-plus-handler installation forwards with an empty name, and chained installation forwards as a chained handler.

Default architecture hooks do nothing except report absence of quiescent state. Hooks arch_enter_from_user_mode with arch_exit_to_user_mode_work and arch_exit_to_user_mode_prepare plus arch_exit_to_user_mode are empty, and arch_in_rcu_eqs reports false, so generic code governs unless overridden. Conditional rescheduling selects per build among a static call, a dynamic dispatch and a raw call, with dynamic enabled mapping to raw and dynamic disabled mapping to null.

Tickless user preparation via tick_nohz_user_enter_prepare flushes deferred wakeups only on full tickless CPUs. The full-CPU test via tick_nohz_full_cpu checks an enabled flag plus mask membership in one variant and always reports false in the other.

Nesting beyond interrupt context and re-entry with mismatched state are guarded. Local disable warns once when called in non-maskable context. User and kernel exit helpers assert disabled interrupts and sane mappings before returning, and the kernel enter path forces context entry on idle or quiescent-state hits so nested ticks cannot falsely claim quiescent state.
